A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, 16 figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–D. The complete material supports comparison, including identification of internal inconsistencies.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D report original LQR and consumption-investment experiments, including approximation errors, runtimes, convergence curves, and policy estimates.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments on both control problems, with numerical outcomes in Table 1 and the experimental figures throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Appendices B and D change the reported consumption-investment control output activation from sigmoid to softplus, permitting outputs above one. This is a limited architecture adaptation; the GPI-PINN and GPI-CBU update procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D revises the financial control task by replacing the admissible set (0,1)^(n+1) with R_+^(n+1), removing unit upper bounds on consumption and individual stock allocations. The LQR and constant/stochastic-coefficient financial scenarios otherwise remain.

E2.justification: The GPI-PINN/GPI-CBU comparisons and Figure 3's PPO, SAC, and Han and E (2016) comparators remain. Analytical and Runge–Kutta references were already used in v2; their revised labeling does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C replaces uniformly sampled entries of the diffusion matrix and jump covariance with B = I_d and standard normal jumps. Appendix D.1 changes the specified utility power from 0.3 to 0.7. These materially revise settings across the principal benchmarks, although the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The jump-intensity sensitivity study in Appendix D.2 has revised reported policy magnitudes: Figure 16 now shows the first stock allocation exceeding one, whereas v2 shows a plateau near one. The intensity sweep, other sensitivity evidence, convergence analyses, and error heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard-deviation bands and describe 10 independent runs for the consumption-investment experiments. No repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or statistical testing practices are added or changed.

E6.justification: Figure 16's right-hand vertical scale changes from 0–1.0 to 0–1.5 while retaining the curve geometry, changing reported policy values, including the first allocation's plateau from approximately 1 to 1.5. Table 1 and the remaining plotted numerical values are retained. The revised control specifications preclude interpreting this as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds missing terminal discount factors and revises the formal admissible control set and CRRA utility formulation. The main theorems and Propositions 3.1 and 4.1 remain; Appendix A's proof edits largely reorganize equivalent algebra and notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: two model-based neural policy-iteration algorithms, global value/control approximation, and efficient high-dimensional jump handling through GPI-CBU.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C correct v2's general analytical/closed-form characterization of LQR references: v3 distinguishes closed-form solutions when Λ2 = 0 from Runge–Kutta references for controlled intensity. The principal mechanism explanations and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes Appendix B's explicit per-gradient minibatch-resampling and total-batch-size explanation. Appendix C replaces explicit time/state and terminal sampling distributions with a citation. Code-link, hardware, learning-rate, and network-size disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kingma and Ba (2014) for the already-used Adam optimizer and an introductory reference to Dupret and Hainaut (2024), already cited elsewhere in v2. The broader positioning against model-free RL and PDE-solving approaches remains.

P1.justification: There is copyediting and localized rewriting of the introduction, experiment descriptions, and appendices, plus terminology cleanup and replacement of the preprint notice with the NeurIPS 2025 notice. The overall section hierarchy and narrative remain.

P2.justification: Figures, algorithms, and the table are retained but relocated, with edited legends, captions, and table headings. Figure 16's vertical tick labels change. New caption conflicts include Figure 6's d = 10 versus the surrounding d = 50 description, and Figure 10's constant-intensity parameters versus its controlled-intensity discussion.

improvement.justification: Useful corrections to LQR reference descriptions and terminal discounting are outweighed by new inconsistencies. v2's Figure 12 endpoint V(1,50) ≈ 10.8 matches its utility power 0.3; v3 retains that endpoint while specifying power 0.7, whose terminal condition requires approximately 22.1. Conflicting LQR captions and removed sampling specifications further weaken experimental validation and reproducibility, producing a limited overall decline.
